pinterest.title: Brazilian Wedding Traditions: From Noivado to Bem-Casados
pinterest.description: A guide to Brazilian wedding traditions in the order they tend to happen: the noivado, the chá de panela, padrinhos and madrinhas, names written inside the bride's hem, the groom's tie cut into keepsakes and bem-casados handed to guests as they leave. Customs vary by region, by faith and by family, so treat them as a menu to discuss with both families. Includes notes for Australians marrying legally in Brazil.

pinterest.title: Brazilian Wedding Ring Finger: Why the Aliança Moves Hands
pinterest.description: Many Brazilian couples wear the aliança on the right hand while engaged and move it to the left hand during the wedding. It is often told that the move marks the moment the promise becomes a marriage. Many couples also choose matching bands, so both partners wear one through the engagement. Read more Brazilian wedding traditions and what they mean.

pinterest.title: Bem-Casados: The Brazilian Wedding Sweet Whose Name Means Well Married
pinterest.description: A bem-casado is a small, soft sponge cake made of two halves. It is often told that the joined halves stand for the couple and that eating one wishes them a good marriage, which is why many couples wrap each one and hand them to guests as they leave. They usually sit beside docinhos such as brigadeiros. Tip: outside Brazil, find a baker who has made bem-casados before and taste a batch well ahead.

slides: Brazilian wedding traditions you did not know, in the order they tend to happen
Noivado: the engagement is often marked with a party. Many couples wear the aliança on the right hand, then move it to the left during the wedding.
Chá de panela: a gathering where the bride receives gifts for her new home. Also called chá de cozinha, a kitchen tea.
Padrinhos and madrinhas are formal witnesses to the wedding. Choose them for the role, not only for the photographs.
Names inside the dress: the bride writes unmarried friends' names inside her hem. It is often told that whoever's name has worn away will be the next to marry.
Bem-casados: a small sponge cake of two halves, handed to guests as they leave. The name translates as "well married".
Customs vary by region, by faith and by family. Treat them as a menu to discuss with both families, not a checklist.

instagram_carousel.caption:
A Brazilian wedding usually starts long before the ceremony. There is an engagement that families mark, a gathering of gifts for the new home, and a group of sponsors chosen with real care.

Swipe for the customs, from the noivado to the bem-casados handed out as guests leave. We say plainly which meanings are documented and which are simply often told.

Lighter customs include Santo Antônio's June festivities, unmarried friends' names written inside the bride's hem and the groom's tie cut into keepsakes.

Brazil is a large country, and its weddings are not one national style. Customs vary by region, by faith and, above all, by family. The ones that travel best need nothing but people: padrinhos and madrinhas, alianças moved from right hand to left during the vows, names inside a hem and a table of bem-casados by the door.

Marrying in Brazil as an Australian? The full guide covers the cartório, documents and Smartraveller notes. Link in bio.

Which tradition would you keep? Tell us in the comments, or send us a message to speak with a Wedded Advisor.
